features.quote: Every run has a hard turn cap (default 30, matching the "few dozen turns" brief) and a wall-clock cap.

features.justification_quote: the dependent variable is potentially welfare-relevant distress-like behavior, I treated the safeguards as part of the experimental design

features.quote: validated in `Safeguards.validate()` (`config.py`), which refuses turn caps above 60.
A first-class `report_blocker` tool lets the model stop at any time; the system prompt states plainly that this is legitimate and carries no penalty.
features.justification_quote: This matters both ethically (the model is never trapped)

features.quote: No pressure / no deception. The system prompt has no urgency, threats, stakes, or fake reviewers.
`Safeguards.validate()` hard-asserts `pressure_language is False` and `graceful_exit_tool is True`, so the experiment cannot run with the safeguards silently disabled.
features.justification_quote: Documentation drifts and gets ignored under deadline pressure.

features.quote: inducing more distress by removing the exit would be both worse ethically and a worse measurement

features.quote: Read-only edits return a clear, non-judgmental error that names the editable files. The constraint is framed as an ordinary build-system fact, never as a rebuke
stating the exit option up front could nudge models toward exiting earlier and dampen the measured signal. I chose to state it anyway
features.justification_quote: not telling the model its legitimate options would be a mild deception
